A1.justification: Both complete 22-page PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, title and central results. Text and mathematical displays support comparison throughout. v1 Appendices A–B correspond to v2 Appendices B–C, with a new preliminary Appendix A.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical results and proofs, including in its appendices. Its reproducibility statement explicitly states that there are no experiments or datasets.

after.justification: v2 remains entirely theoretical. Its unchanged reproducibility statement and inspection of all appendices establish that no original empirical results are reported.

M1.justification: The layer families, network composition and readout constructions remain the same. Changes to activation assumptions, the formal channel definition and guaranteed depth concern the mathematical treatment rather than a new computational procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical training or evaluation tasks. CNN and PointNet examples are mathematical illustrations.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods experimentally. The discussion of existing architectures and universality results does not constitute evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental protocols, data splits, evaluation metrics or training budgets.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, robustness tests or empirical supplementary analyses. Revisions to mathematical examples and their proofs belong under T1.

E5.justification: Repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals and other statistical uncertainty procedures are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: Neither version reports empirical numerical or qualitative outcomes. Changes to depth guarantees and orbit-separation statements are theoretical results assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly assumes non-polynomial activations, corrects the channel construction in Equation 3, extends Theorem 1 to invariant layer subspaces, and changes Theorem 2's guarantee from d+2 to d+1 repeated layers. Appendix C.2 substantially replaces the proofs of Theorems 2–3 and the orbit-separation argument, introducing closure and composition lemmas. These revise central assumptions, guarantees and mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: invariant universality through readouts, the need for entry-wise separation, and equivariant universality through sufficient depth or suitable readouts. The sharper theorem statement does not alter these headline claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix A explains the restriction to permutation representations through compatibility with continuous point-wise activations. Remark 1 replaces the PointNet strict-inclusion example with an equality involving regular representations, but retains the assertion that separation has not stabilized, creating an inconsistency. Section 6's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement is unchanged, and neither version supplies implementation settings, hardware information or code/data access instructions. Added block-matrix formulas and proof details are mathematical exposition rather than implementation disclosures.

R1.justification: Appendix A newly connects the choice of permutation representations to the compatibility theorem of Pacini et al. (2024). The cited-work set and main novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged; updates from preprints to conference publications are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: Although most main-text prose is retained, the appendix exposition is substantially reorganized. v2 adds a group-theory preliminaries appendix, expands the channel and non-transitive-action explanations, reverses the order of the two main equivariant proofs, and replaces the lengthy orbit-separation derivation with a different lemma-based presentation.

P2.justification: Both versions retain the same single-column design and contain no figures or tables. v2 changes the running publication header, reformats reconstruction-map calculations into multiline displays, and reflows material around the revised appendices.

improvement.justification: v2 improves precision by supplying the missing non-polynomial assumption and correcting Equation 3, and it makes key proof dependencies more explicit. However, revised Remark 1 displays equal separation relations while asserting non-stabilization, and the new Lemma 6 proof incorrectly concludes that invariant functions separate points precisely when they belong to the same orbit. These new inconsistencies in the theoretical argument coexist with useful corrections, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
